classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied quartiles to calculate the IQR and both outlier fences, then compare each candidate with those bounds. This is a short routine chain with no need to organise data or choose a method.

content.prompt: The lower and upper quartiles for a data set are 116 and 134. Which of the following data values would be classified as an outlier?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=134-116\\\text{IQR}&=18\\1.5\times\text{IQR}&=27\\\text{Lower fence}&=116-27\\\text{Lower fence}&=89\\\text{Upper fence}&=134+27\\\text{Upper fence}&=161\end{align*}$$

Since $190>161$, it is an outlier.

$$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=134-116\\\text{IQR}&=18\\1.5\times\text{IQR}&=27\\\text{Lower fence}&=116-27\\\text{Lower fence}&=89\\\text{Upper fence}&=134+27\\\text{Upper fence}&=161\end{align*}$$

Since $60<89$, it is an outlier.

$$\begin{align*}\text{IQR}&=134-116\\\text{IQR}&=18\\1.5\times\text{IQR}&=27\\\text{Lower fence}&=116-27\\\text{Lower fence}&=89\\\text{Upper fence}&=134+27\\\text{Upper fence}&=161\end{align*}$$

Since $150$ lies between the fences, it is not an outlier.
